title: New pleasure with freedom to finish

captions.physics: Changing the familiar view of leisure
captions.energy: Wanting an increasingly rich new experience
captions.emotions: Holding onto promised fullness of enjoyment

meaning: Freedom to finish supports leisure when changing a familiar form produces another programme that becomes difficult to release.
text: Changing familiar leisure does not automatically free it from demands. The Hanged Man in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes pausing an earlier script and looking differently at pleasure. The Empress in energy leans towards making the new form richer. The Devil in emotions holds promised fullness: releasing one part seems to lose the whole. A free change of perspective risks ending in another obligation. Both need to hear what actually delights now, beyond preserving initial excitement through a greater quantity of experiences.

Suppose you replace a shopping walk with trying amusing outfits from old clothes at home. Music, photographs and several more costumes join the idea. **A new pleasure remains free while its scale can shrink.** One funny outfit can already delight both. Remaining clothes become no debt, and prepared variety requires no compulsory use. You can keep the enjoyment and hear a wish to finish even while some planned details never receive a turn.

The difficulty is justifying continuation through how much has been imagined. The script changed, but a programme again replaces living interest. Richness determines whether the evening counts as successful, and stopping causes hurt. Another perspective helps when applied to the new idea too. Free participation matters more than complete performance. You can choose less, postpone or never return without devaluing the play already shared.
